scope: Proposition 5.4 (Conditioning, aborts, and completed-output limits) of the manuscript “Entanglement with zero distillable secret key in local dimension ten” (preprints/Entanglement-with-zero-distillable-secret-key-in-local-dimension-ten-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 272 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 be18f63c5a1d11a2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: Consider inputs ω⊗n with ω ∈ C and n ≥ 1, and admitted protocols whose normalized completed outputs retain in Eve’s register an arbitrary initial purification and the complete public transcript. The following statements extend the gap in Theorem 5.3; in item 2, the completed local output alphabet may include an abort symbol. 1. If A is a measurable event of the complete public transcript with probability r > 0, the normalized bit output conditioned on A has distance at least 1/5 from every ideal bit law for that accepted output. This holds for every r > 0. 2. Suppose a sequence of completed protocols has a locally available abort symbol at either party. If the probability that at least one party aborts tends to zero, and the normalized non-aborting outputs approach ideal non-aborting bit laws, then replacing each local abort by the fixed bit zero would give completed bit outputs approaching ideal bits. Such a sequence is impossible for inputs in C (including any numbers of copies). 3. Let τk be completed normalized bit outputs to which the gap applies, possibly on different output spaces. Suppose their bit registers are kept fixed and their Eve registers are embedded in a common output space F, giving states b τk. The embeddings must preserve and permit recovery of the full initial purification and complete public records, without coarse-graining those records. In particular, an Eve-side recovery channel recovers τk from b τk while leaving the bits fixed. If b τk → τ in trace norm, then for every normalized law σF , τ − 1 2 1 X i=0 |i, i⟩⟨i, i| ⊗ σF 1 ≥ 1 5 .
